root_cause.text: `__do_adjtimex()` in `kernel/time/timekeeping.c` incorrectly used the global `tk_core` timekeeper when updating leap state, so adjtimex calls on an auxiliary timekeeper modified the wrong `tk_data`/seqlock without the proper lock held.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);` to `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd);`, and the CVE text says that when `__do_ajdtimex()` was used for an auxiliary timekeeper, “the core timekeeper would be updated incorrectly” and this triggered “the timekeepers sequence lock gets written to without holding its associated spinlock.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the current timekeeping data instance when updating leap state in adjtimex handling.
intent_record.what: In __do_adjtimex(), the call to tk_update_leap_state_all() was changed from passing &tk_core to passing the local tkd pointer.
intent_record.how: This makes the leap-state update operate on the specific timekeeping data instance associated with the current operation instead of always using the global tk_core object, ensuring the update is applied to the intended clock state.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes adjtimex leap-state updates to use the current timekeeping instance instead of the global tk_core, preventing updates to the wrong tk_data/seqlock.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit ae455cb7b8ad2c1a3947394d448912fa2385f7d2
Author: Anna-Maria Behnsen <anna-maria@linutronix.de>
Date:   Wed Oct 9 10:29:16 2024 +0200

    timekeeping: Rework do_adjtimex() to use shadow_timekeeper
    
    Updates of the timekeeper can be done by operating on the shadow timekeeper
    and afterwards copying the result into the real timekeeper. This has the
    advantage, that the sequence count write protected region is kept as small
    as possible.
    
    Convert do_adjtimex() to use
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this function body. The root cause was that `__do_adjtimex()` updated leap state using the global real timekeeper (`tk_core.timekeeper`) instead of the auxiliary/shadow timekeeper, which could touch the wrong `tk_data`/seqlock. In this commit, `do_adjtimex()` explicitly operates on the shadow timekeeper: `struct timekeeper *tks = &tk_core.shadow_timekeeper;` and `orig_tai = tai = tks->tai_offset;`. On the update path it calls `__timekeeping_set_tai_offset(tks, tai);` and `timekeeping_update_from_shadow(&tk_core, TK_CLOCK_WAS_SET);`, and on the non-TAI-change path it uses `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);`, which updates both shadow and real timekeeper under `write_seqcount_begin(&tkd->seq)`. This shows the old incorrect direct use of the global timekeeper has been replaced by the shadow-timekeeper-based fix.
